job.title: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
job.description:
Our client is building dedicated GPU infrastructure for demanding AI workloads. From their base in Australia, they support organisations and distributed teams across global markets, with a particular focus on Europe. Their NeoCloud proposition covers AI training, fine-tuning, inference and data-intensive workloads. It brings together bare-metal GPU capacity, high-speed networking and storage, secure access, hybrid integration, monitoring and ongoing operations.

They are seeking a Chief Technology Officer to lead this business end to end.

This is not a strategy-only CTO position. You will be accountable for the architecture, deployment and operation of their NeoCloud platform. You will set the technical direction, build the team and operating model, guide infrastructure investment, support strategic customers and ensure that every production commitment is technically sound, operationally supportable and commercially sensible.

What you will own

You will lead the full infrastructure lifecycle, from workload discovery and capacity planning through architecture, procurement, commissioning, customer onboarding and production operations. Your remit will include:

  • the technical strategy, roadmap and reference architecture for the NeoCloud platform;
  • GPU compute, high-performance networking, storage, platform software, automation, observability and security;
  • data-centre and deployment readiness, hardware integration, benchmarking, acceptance and production handover;
  • service reliability, performance, capacity, incident response, change control, business continuity and operational support;
  • customer solution design, technical due diligence, onboarding and senior technical engagement;
  • GPU utilisation, deployment economics, technology refresh and supplier performance; and
  • the recruitment, leadership and development of a high-calibre infrastructure, platform and operations team.

You will work closely with the CEO on investment priorities, partnerships, major customer commitments and business growth. You will also be expected to remain close to the technology: reviewing architecture, resolving difficult delivery decisions and taking command when a major production issue demands senior ownership.

What you will bring

You will have led both the build and operation of production-grade infrastructure in GPU cloud, high-performance computing, cloud infrastructure, data centres, hosting, telecommunications or a closely related field. You will combine executive leadership with genuine technical depth across bare-metal compute, Linux, networking, storage, orchestration, automation, observability, identity and security.

You should be able to demonstrate that you have:

  • taken complex infrastructure from design and procurement into reliable live operation;
  • led production operations with accountability for availability, performance, incidents, capacity and cost;
  • worked directly with GPU or other accelerator platforms and understand the demands of distributed AI workloads;
  • improved reliability, utilisation, deployment speed or unit economics through measurable action;
  • built and led strong engineering and operations teams;
  • made sound commercial decisions involving capital, suppliers, customer requirements and delivery risk; and
  • communicated credibly with engineers, enterprise customers, executives, investors and strategic partners.

Experience with multi-node GPU clusters, high-bandwidth Ethernet, RoCE or InfiniBand, scalable storage, Kubernetes or Slurm, and the NVIDIA or AMD accelerator ecosystem would be valuable. So would experience with high-density data-centre deployment, enterprise security, multi-tenant infrastructure or international operations.

Formal qualifications are welcome, but they are not a substitute for evidence that you have built and operated critical infrastructure successfully.

The person we are looking for

You will bring clarity to difficult decisions and own the consequences. You will be rigorous without becoming bureaucratic, commercially grounded without compromising operational integrity, and confident enough to invite challenge from strong specialists. You will know when to design for the future and when to solve today’s problem simply and reliably.

Most importantly, you will understand that a GPU infrastructure company succeeds through execution. Capacity must arrive when promised. Clusters must perform consistently. Customers must be onboarded safely. Incidents must be managed decisively. Capital must be deployed with discipline.

Our client’s proposition is straightforward: technology should be planned, supplied, deployed and supported as one accountable service.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the platform, organisation and operating model of a growing infrastructure business. The scope is broad, the standards are high and the outcomes will be visible.

job.title: CEO (Hong Kong SME)
job.description:
International specialist electronics business | Founder transition

We are retained to appoint the next Chief Executive Officer of an established Hong Kong-based company that develops and supplies specialist electronic products to international markets.

This SME sells primarily through a global network of distributors, serving institutional and consumer applications in a quality-sensitive specialist sector. The company has an established product portfolio, proprietary technical know-how, long-standing channel relationships and an experienced team.

The founder is preparing to retire. This appointment is therefore both a leadership succession and a business transformation mandate. The incoming CEO will take full executive responsibility, manage an orderly transfer of founder-held knowledge and relationships, and prepare the company for its next stage of sustainable international growth.

The role

Reporting to the Board, the CEO will assume end-to-end responsibility for the profit and loss account, strategy, people, commercial performance, products and operations.

The immediate priority will be to maintain continuity and confidence throughout the founder transition. This will require a disciplined handover of key customer and distributor relationships, technical and market knowledge, operating responsibilities and decision rights.

Beyond the transition, the CEO will assess where the company can compete and grow most effectively. They will sharpen the commercial plan, strengthen the management of international distributors and focus resources on the markets, partners and products with the best potential. They will also improve forecasting, management information and accountability while keeping systems and processes proportionate to an SME.

The CEO will work closely with commercial and technical colleagues to guide the product roadmap. The successful candidate does not need to be an engineer, but must understand technical products well enough to ask incisive questions, contribute to development priorities and engage credibly in technical discussions with customers and channel partners.

This is a hands-on role. The appointee must be willing to move between Board discussions and operating detail, including distributor reviews, key account conversations, pricing and margin decisions, product trade-offs, team development and delivery issues. It will not suit someone who relies on the infrastructure or functional depth of a large multinational.

Candidate profile

Candidates should be able to demonstrate:

  • General management or business-unit leadership with meaningful profit-and-loss accountability.
  • Success managing and developing international distributors, dealers or channel partners across multiple markets.
  • Strong people leadership and the ability to guide an organisation through succession, transformation or another period of material change.
  • Experience with technical, engineered or electronic products. An engineering qualification is not required, but technical curiosity and product judgement are essential.
  • Sound commercial judgement across sales, pricing, margin, product portfolio and market-development decisions.
  • The ability to turn strategy into execution in a resource-conscious SME environment.
  • Credibility across cultures both internally and externally.
  • The ability and commitment to be based in Hong Kong.

Exposure to product development, outsourced manufacturing or supply chains in Asia would be advantageous.

The strongest candidates are likely to combine commercial drive with practical operating discipline. They will be direct, low-ego and technically curious. They must be able to respect the company’s history while making clear decisions about what should change.

Why consider the opportunity?

This is a genuine CEO mandate with the opportunity to shape an established international business at an important point in its development. The incoming leader will inherit a credible platform rather than a turnaround situation, but will have meaningful scope to strengthen the organisation, improve channel performance and set the direction for the post-founder era.

job.title: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
job.description:
Our client is building dedicated GPU infrastructure for demanding AI workloads. From their base in Australia, they support organisations and distributed teams across global markets, with a particular focus on Europe. It brings together bare-metal GPU capacity, high-speed networking and storage, secure access, hybrid integration, monitoring and ongoing operations.

They are seeking a Chief Technology Officer to lead this business end to end.

This is not a strategy-only CTO position. You will be accountable for the architecture, deployment and operation of their NeoCloud platform. You will set the technical direction, build the team and operating model, guide infrastructure investment, support strategic customers and ensure that every production commitment is technically sound, operationally supportable and commercially sensible.

What you will own

You will lead the full infrastructure lifecycle, from workload discovery and capacity planning through architecture, procurement, commissioning, customer onboarding and production operations. Your remit will include:

  • the technical strategy, roadmap and reference architecture for the NeoCloud platform;
  • GPU compute, high-performance networking, storage, platform software, automation, observability and security;
  • data-centre and deployment readiness, hardware integration, benchmarking, acceptance and production handover;
  • service reliability, performance, capacity, incident response, change control, business continuity and operational support;
  • customer solution design, technical due diligence, onboarding and senior technical engagement;
  • GPU utilisation, deployment economics, technology refresh and supplier performance; and
  • the recruitment, leadership and development of a high-calibre infrastructure, platform and operations team.

You will work closely with the CEO on investment priorities, partnerships, major customer commitments and business growth. You will also be expected to remain close to the technology: reviewing architecture, resolving difficult delivery decisions and taking command when a major production issue demands senior ownership.

What you will bring

You will have led both the build and operation of production-grade infrastructure in GPU cloud, high-performance computing, cloud infrastructure, data centres, hosting, telecommunications or a closely related field. You will combine executive leadership with genuine technical depth across bare-metal compute, Linux, networking, storage, orchestration, automation, observability, identity and security.

You should be able to demonstrate that you have:

  • taken complex infrastructure from design and procurement into reliable live operation;
  • led production operations with accountability for availability, performance, incidents, capacity and cost;
  • worked directly with GPU or other accelerator platforms and understand the demands of distributed AI workloads;
  • improved reliability, utilisation, deployment speed or unit economics through measurable action;
  • built and led strong engineering and operations teams;
  • made sound commercial decisions involving capital, suppliers, customer requirements and delivery risk; and
  • communicated credibly with engineers, enterprise customers, executives, investors and strategic partners.

Experience with multi-node GPU clusters, high-bandwidth Ethernet, RoCE or InfiniBand, scalable storage, Kubernetes or Slurm, and the NVIDIA or AMD accelerator ecosystem would be valuable. So would experience with high-density data-centre deployment, enterprise security, multi-tenant infrastructure or international operations.

Formal qualifications are welcome, but they are not a substitute for evidence that you have built and operated critical infrastructure successfully.

The person we are looking for

You will bring clarity to difficult decisions and own the consequences. You will be rigorous without becoming bureaucratic, commercially grounded without compromising operational integrity, and confident enough to invite challenge from strong specialists. You will know when to design for the future and when to solve today’s problem simply and reliably.

Most importantly, you will understand that a GPU infrastructure company succeeds through execution. Capacity must arrive when promised. Clusters must perform consistently. Customers must be onboarded safely. Incidents must be managed decisively. Capital must be deployed with discipline.

Our client’s proposition is straightforward: technology should be planned, supplied, deployed and supported as one accountable service.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the platform, organisation and operating model of a growing infrastructure business. The scope is broad, the standards are high and the outcomes will be visible.
